skill.name: database-design
skill.description: Design database schemas, select databases and ORMs, plan indexes and migrations, optimize queries, and validate Prisma schemas.
skill.summary: Make context-aware database architecture decisions and identify common schema problems.

content.value_statement: Database choices often ignore workload, deployment, and migration constraints. This skill guides selection, schema design, indexing, optimization, and safer changes.
actual_capabilities: Compares PostgreSQL, Neon, Turso, SQLite, PlanetScale, and CockroachDB for common deployment requirements.
Guides normalization, primary key selection, timestamps, relationships, and foreign key deletion behavior.
Recommends index types and composite index ordering based on query patterns.
Explains N+1 prevention, execution plan review, selective columns, pagination, and caching priorities.
Outlines staged migration patterns for columns, indexes, renames, and zero-downtime changes.
Scans up to ten local Prisma or Drizzle schema files and reports common Prisma issues.
limitations: Database recommendations are general guidance and require validation against real workload, cost, and operational constraints.
The validator performs detailed checks only for Prisma schemas; discovered Drizzle files receive no validation.
The validator uses regular expressions, so it cannot fully parse every valid Prisma schema.
Validation reports warnings and exits successfully, even when schema issues are found.

use_cases.title: Choose a Database Stack
use_cases.description: Compare database and ORM options against deployment, latency, query, scaling, and developer experience requirements.

use_cases.title: Review a New Schema
use_cases.description: Evaluate entities, keys, relationships, timestamps, normalization, and indexes before implementation.

use_cases.title: Plan Production Changes
use_cases.description: Prepare staged migrations and query improvements that reduce locking, downtime, and performance regressions.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Database
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose a database for [application]. Requirements include [deployment], [traffic], [query needs], and [availability]. Compare suitable options and explain trade-offs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner selection for a new application

prompt_templates.title: Design a Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a schema for [domain]. Include entities, primary keys, relationships, deletion behavior, timestamps, normalization choices, and expected access patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Review Indexes and Queries
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these tables and query patterns: [details]. Recommend indexes, identify N+1 risks, and explain what to verify with execution plans.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a zero-downtime migration plan for [change]. Account for [database], [table size], [deployment process], rollback, backfill, locking, and compatibility.

output_examples.input: Select storage for a small local desktop application with simple relational data and one writer.
output: Reasoning: Embedded storage and single-writer access match the stated workload.
Trade-off: Reassess if concurrent writes or global distribution become requirements.

output_examples.input: Review an orders table queried by customer, status, and creation date.
output: Start with an index aligned to the most frequent customer and status filter.
Place equality columns before the creation-date range column.
Confirm the choice with an execution plan and production-like data.

output_examples.input: Add a required column to a large production table without downtime.
output: Add the column as nullable first.
Backfill existing rows in controlled batches.
Deploy compatible application code, then add the required constraint.
Prepare rollback steps before each stage.

best_practices: Provide deployment, workload, consistency, latency, and growth requirements before requesting a recommendation.
Share representative queries and data volumes when planning indexes or optimization.
Test migrations on a realistic data copy and verify rollback procedures before production.
anti_patterns: Do not choose PostgreSQL or any ORM without comparing requirements and operational trade-offs.
Do not add indexes without considering write cost, selectivity, and actual query patterns.
Do not perform breaking schema changes in one deployment step.

faq.question: Does this skill generate complete production SQL?
faq.answer: It provides design guidance and may suggest structures, but production SQL still requires database-specific review and testing.

faq.question: Which databases does it compare?
faq.answer: It covers PostgreSQL, Neon, Turso, SQLite, PlanetScale, and CockroachDB in its selection guidance.

faq.question: Which ORMs does it discuss?
faq.answer: It compares Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely, raw SQL, and SQLAlchemy for different deployment and development needs.

faq.question: Can it validate Drizzle schemas?
faq.answer: The script discovers likely Drizzle files, but detailed Drizzle validation is not implemented.

faq.question: Does the Prisma validator modify files?
faq.answer: No. It reads matching schema files and prints warnings without changing project content.

faq.question: Can it guarantee zero-downtime migrations?
faq.answer: No. It outlines safer stages, but guarantees require testing against the actual database, data volume, traffic, and deployment process.
